# cookiecutter-rt-django Changelog

Main purpose of this file is to provide a changelog for the template itself.
It is not intended to be used as a changelog for the generated project.

This changelog will document any know **BREAKING** changes between versions of the template.
Please review this new entries carefully after applying `cruft update` before committing the changes.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/).

Currently, `cookiecutter-rt-django` has no explicit versioning amd we purely rely on `cruft` diff.

## [Unreleased]

* **Security (eMudhra / emSign CA incident, follow-up 2)**: `letsencrypt_setup.sh` issues certificates with `nginx-rt:v1.4.0` instead of `v1.2.2`, whose certbot still trusted the compromised CA. The backups email helper now verifies the SMTP server certificate (`starttls()` used no verification before), and the backups image requires `certifi>=2026.10.19`. The AWS deploy workflow upgrades the runner's `ca-certificates` and points AWS CLI at the system store (`AWS_CA_BUNDLE`); the AWS keys are only exposed to the deploy step. `bin/prepare-os.sh` installs or upgrades `ca-certificates` first, so everything it downloads afterwards uses an up-to-date CA bundle; it no longer installs `sentry-cli` or the `b2` CLI on the host (the backups container ships its own), and it checks the Docker apt key fingerprint. AWS `cloud-init.yml` checks the AWS CLI signature and the Docker apt key fingerprint. CI uses `astral-sh/setup-uv` v10.3.2 without a fixed uv version, `[tool.uv] required-version = ">=0.13.4"` makes local `uv` fail if it is older, and all actions are pinned to commit SHAs (Dependabot raises no alerts for SHA-pinned actions). Terraform now requires `>= 1.16.7, < 2.0.0` (older releases are built with a Go that lacks the CA distrust). `README_AWS.md` asks for AWS CLI ≥ 2.38.4 (older versions bundle a CA list that trusts the compromised CA). Dependabot no longer watches Docker images (GitHub has no security advisories for images, so the entry could only open version-update PRs); Python packages stay security-only. **Existing projects updating with `cruft update`:** apply the workflow changes by hand if the update PR cannot push them (the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot modify workflows); on AWS, upgrade Terraform before the next `terraform apply`; on existing direct hosts, upgrade `ca-certificates`, `docker-ce` / `containerd.io` and the AWS CLI (≥ 2.38.4) through host maintenance, since `prepare-os.sh` only runs at setup. Leftover `sentry-cli` and `b2` binaries on existing hosts are not removed.
* **BREAKING** Removed Packer and Vultr support: the `vultr` choice of `deployment_type` and the `aws_use_packer` option are gone, together with `devops/packer/`, `devops/vultr_scripts/`, `devops/vultr_tf/` and `README_vultr.md`. AWS instances always boot the stock Ubuntu 24.04 minimal AMI and cloud-init runs `installer.sh` on first boot. **Existing projects updating with `cruft update`:** Vultr projects must switch to the `direct` deployment type (`cruft update --variables-to-update '{ "deployment_type": "direct" }'`), otherwise cookiecutter rejects the stale choice; the update deletes the Vultr files, reject those deletions to keep them. AWS projects that used Packer lose the Packer files and now run `installer.sh` on every new instance; to move to the stock AMI set `aws_ami_image` to `*ubuntu-noble-24.04-amd64-minimal-*` and `aws_ami_image_owner` to `099720109477` (e.g. via `--variables-to-update`), run `terraform apply` and refresh the instances. The stale `aws_use_packer` key in `.cruft.json` is harmless.
* **BREAKING** Removed vulnerability scanning: the `vulnerabilities_scanning` cookiecutter option and the `vulnrelay` and `watchtower` services (prod and AWS compose) are gone, together with `envs/prod/.vuln.env.template`, the `.vuln.env` handling in `setup-prod.sh` and the "Vulnerability scanning" section of `README_AWS.md`. node-exporter now always reads textfile metrics from the `nodeexporter_collectors` volume (mounted at `/textfile_collectors`), which stays available for project-specific `.prom` files. `deploy.sh` now runs `docker compose up -d --remove-orphans`, so containers of services no longer in `docker-compose.yml` are removed on deploy — including containers started by hand within the same compose project (e.g. `docker compose run` without `--rm`). **Existing projects updating with `cruft update`:** the stale `vulnerabilities_scanning` key in `.cruft.json` is harmless. On direct/vultr deployments the next `deploy.sh` removes the `vulnrelay` and `watchtower` containers; afterwards delete `envs/prod/.vuln.env` and the `.vuln.env` symlink in the project root. On AWS, refresh the instances and delete the `/application/<name>/<env>/.vuln.env` SSM parameter (cloud-init downloads every parameter under that path). Finally, retire the project's product in DefectDojo.
* **Security (eMudhra / emSign CA incident, follow-up)**: deployments now refresh images instead of reusing stale cached ones, so fixed base images and CA bundles are picked up. `deploy.sh` builds with `--pull` and runs `docker compose pull --ignore-buildable` before `up -d`; `devops/scripts/build-backend.sh` builds with `--pull`. The services that reuse the locally built app image (`celery-worker`, `celery-beat`, `celery-flower`) are marked `pull_policy: never` so the pull step skips them. Bumped `grafana/alloy` `v1.15.1` → `v1.21.1` and `nginx-rt` `v1.3.0` → `v1.4.0` (prod and AWS compose), and `postgres:14.0-alpine` → `postgres:14-alpine` (prod and dev; a minor upgrade within PostgreSQL 14, no dump/restore needed). **Existing projects updating with `cruft update`:** check that a custom `alloy/config.alloy` still loads under Alloy v1.21, then redeploy.
* **Security (eMudhra / emSign CA incident, [advisory](https://discuss.python.org/t/information-for-python-users-regarding-emudhra-emsign-ca-certificate-security-incident/109576))**: `certifi>=2026.10.19` is now a uv constraint and is exempt from the `exclude-newer` cooldown; uv is pinned to `0.13.4` in the prod Dockerfile and CI. **Existing projects updating with `cruft update`:** run `uv lock` and commit the result — the prod image installs with `uv sync --frozen`, so rebuilding without re-locking still ships the old certifi. If your `[tool.uv]` section or CI differs from the template, apply the same changes by hand. Then rebuild and redeploy.
* postgres-exporter connects to `${POSTGRES_HOST}:${POSTGRES_PORT}` instead of a hardcoded `db:5432`. Defaults in `.env` are unchanged (`db` / `5432`, `sslmode=disable` for the bundled container). Hosted databases that require TLS need `sslmode=require` in `DATA_SOURCE_URI`.
* Set cAdvisor's `privileged` option explicitly to `false` in both AWS and regular production. AWS previously enabled privileged mode; check container metric collection on a staging instance before rolling out this change.
* Fixed AWS monitoring: aligned cAdvisor with regular production (`v0.60.5` and host mounts) and exposed the existing PostgreSQL exporter at `/postgres-metrics/` on monitoring port `10443`. Apply the Terraform changes and refresh the EC2 instance to deploy the updated configuration.
* Added PostgreSQL monitoring (enabled with `monitoring`): a `postgres-exporter` container served as `/postgres-metrics/` on the nginx monitoring port (`10443`); the bundled `db` now preloads `pg_stat_statements` (with `track_io_timing=on`) so per-query timings are recorded, in dev too, where there is no exporter but the view can be queried with `psql`. With no configuration the exporter connects as `POSTGRES_USER`; optionally set `POSTGRES_EXPORTER_USER` and `POSTGRES_EXPORTER_PASSWORD` in the deployed environment's `.env` (both or neither) to use a dedicated read-only role instead, created automatically by `db/init/01-monitoring.sh` on a fresh database. **Existing projects updating with `cruft update`:** the next deploy recreates the `db` container to pick up the new `command`, then create the extension by hand — the init script only runs on a fresh data directory (see `db/init/README.md`). `.gitignore` now ignores `/db/data/` instead of `/db/` so `db/init` is tracked. On AWS/RDS the exporter keeps using `DATABASE_URL`. `deploy.sh` now reloads nginx at the end so recreated containers don't leave it proxying to stale IPs.
* **BREAKING** Replaced the `log_aggregating` cookiecutter option with `observability`. Existing projects updating with `cruft update` should set `observability` to `true` if they used log aggregation before, and provide the new `traces_aggregator_url` value plus `TEMPO_URL`, `TEMPO_USER` and `TEMPO_PASSWORD` in production environments.
* **BREAKING** Renamed the `monitor_view_execution_time_in_djagno` cookiecutter option to `monitor_view_execution_time_in_django`; update existing `cruft.json` files or `cruft update --variables-to-update` overrides accordingly.
* **BREAKING** Switched from `pdm` to [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for Python dependency management.
* **BREAKING** Switched from `docker-compose` v1 script to `docker compose` v2 plugin (https://docs.docker.com/compose/cli-command/)
* **BREAKING** Added formatting with ruff.
* **BREAKING** Started using [pdm](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm) for managing Python dependencies.
* **BREAKING** root of repository is used as docker build context instead of just `./app/`.
* **BREAKING** Updated django-environ from 0.4.5 to 0.10 (https://django-environ.readthedocs.io/en/latest/changelog.html)
* **BREAKING** Updated redis python package from 3.5.3 to 4.6 (breaking changes listed in https://github.com/redis/redis-py/releases/tag/v4.0.0b1)
* **BREAKING** Updated Python from 3.9 to 3.11
* **BREAKING** Updated Django from 3.2 to 4.2 (https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.2/releases/4.0/#backwards-incompatible-changes-in-4-0)
* **BREAKING** Updated django-cors-headers from 3.7 to 4.0 (https://github.com/adamchainz/django-cors-headers/blob/main/CHANGELOG.rst#400-2023-05-12)
* **BREAKING** Updated django-environ from 0.7 to 0.10 (https://django-environ.readthedocs.io/en/latest/changelog.html)
* **BREAKING** Updated Python from 3.11 to 3.14
* **BREAKING** Updated Django from 4.2 to 5.2 (https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/releases/5.0/#backwards-incompatible-changes-in-5-0)
* **BREAKING** Updated `cruft.json` variables to boolean types, so `"n"` values are treated as `True` -> when doing cruft update, make sure to update `"n"` variables to `false`, like this:

```sh
cruft update --variables-to-update '{ "use_fingerprinting": false, "use_channels": false, "csp_enabled": false, "nginx_compression_enabled": false, "nginx_tls_early_data_enabled": false, "aws_use_packer": false }'
```
* **BREAKING** Updating to 3.14 causes prometheus files to corrupt and trigger an error:
```
app-1  |   File "/root/src/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/prometheus_client/mmap_dict.py", line 40, in _read_all_values
app-1  |     raise RuntimeError('Read beyond file size detected, file is corrupted.')
```
A simple solution is to stop all containers, remove prometheus data, and start the containers again:
```sh
docker compose stop
rm -rf prometheus-metrics/*
docker compose up -d
```
